exercises.prompt: Identify the grammatical case and marker of مَسَاجِدَ in the phrase below.
choices: Genitive (majrūr) — marked by fatḥah in place of kasrah
exercises.answer: Genitive (majrūr) — marked by fatḥah in place of kasrah
exercises.explanation: مَسَاجِدَ is governed by the preposition فِي (so its case is genitive), but because it is an indefinite diptote on the pattern مَفَاعِلُ, it takes fatḥah in place of kasrah.

feedback.rule: Indefinite, unannexed diptotes take fatḥah as their genitive marker (الفَتْحَةُ نِيَابَةً عَنِ الكَسْرَةِ).
feedback.commonError: Do not call مَسَاجِدَ accusative merely because it ends in fatḥah; the preposition فِي always governs the genitive.

exercises.prompt: Select the correct form of مَسَاجِد when it functions as the muḍāf in an iḍāfah ('in the mosques of the city').
exercises.explanation: Under the diptote reversion rule, serving as the muḍāf of an iḍāfah restores regular genitive kasrah: مَسَاجِدِ.

feedback.rule: Diptotes revert to taking kasrah in the genitive when prefixed by أَلْ or when serving as muḍāf.
feedback.commonError: Leaving fatḥah (مَسَاجِدَ) when annexed violates the diptote reversion rule.

exercises.prompt: True or False: Diptotes (al-mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) accept tanwīn when indefinite.
exercises.explanation: False. 'Al-mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf' literally means barred from tanwīn (nunation) and full three-case inflection.

feedback.commonError: Adding -un or -in to patterns like مَسَاجِدُ or أَكْبَرُ.

exercises.prompt: Match each diptote example to the morphological or semantic reason it is barred from tanwīn.
exercises.explanation: These four represent the most frequent diptote categories in Classical Arabic.
